data.description:
## Context / Problem

rebar is driven by MANY local agent processes at once — high local concurrency is the normal
operating mode, not an edge case. Two 2026-07-31 incidents came from this area, and a third class
remains unaddressed.

Story so far:
- **747f** (closed): an unbounded git call on the materialize path produced 40 sequential per-object
  fetch RPCs and a measured ~2.1-HOUR hang. Fixed with `_GIT_TIMEOUT = 300`.
- **77e1** (closed): bounded the remaining NETWORK-capable git call sites
  (`review_bot/gerrit_client.py`, `opcert_service/workspace.py`) at 300s.
- **304e** (closed): a store write-lock orphaned by a SIGKILLed container became PERMANENTLY
  unreclaimable, because the owner stamp used `socket.gethostname()` — the CONTAINER ID inside a
  container, changing on every recreate — so a same-host orphan was misclassified as the
  foreign-host (shared-filesystem) case.
- **e43f** (open): `run_ensures` burns the full 60s write-lock budget on the BOOT path, which is what
  blew autodeploy's 30s health check during the 304e incident.

**This ticket covers the remaining class: purely LOCAL git operations with NO timeout at all**, run
through module-local `_git` helpers:

- `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py`
- `src/rebar/_commands/delete.py`
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py`   (NOTE: bug 01e8 currently owns this file — coordinate or defer it)
- `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py`
- `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`
- `src/rebar/metrics/blame.py`
- `src/rebar/metrics/git_metrics.py`

A local op cannot hang on the network, so this is materially LOWER severity than 747f/77e1 — which is
why the 77e1 investigator deliberately recorded it rather than fixing it. But it is not zero: under
concurrent local use a local git op can stall on a stuck `index.lock` / `HEAD.lock` /
`packed-refs.lock`, and rebar's whole operating model is concurrent local use.

## Approach — DO NOT bolt on a number before the research lands

The operator has commissioned a research pass on how popular, actively maintained OSS projects handle
LOCAL git contention robustly, specifically covering: local-lock contention handling (retry/backoff
vs serialize vs per-op `GIT_INDEX_FILE`/worktree vs plumbing-only), whether bounding a purely LOCAL
subprocess is normal practice at all, sound stale-lock reclamation (pid+start-time, kernel-mediated
flock, lease/TTL, boot-id), and blocking policy under contention — with prior art from git itself
(`core.filesRefLockTimeout`, `core.packedRefsTimeout`), Mercurial (which hit rebar's EXACT
hostname-identity bug), cargo's package-cache lock, Bazel's output-base lock, git-annex, git-lfs, and
the Python `filelock`/`portalocker` libraries.

**Those findings will be appended to this ticket as a comment and must inform the design.** A blanket
timeout copied from the network sites (300s) is very likely the WRONG answer here: local ops have a
completely different latency profile, and a too-short bound would abort legitimate slow work on a
large repo while a too-long one is indistinguishable from today.

Also in scope, and arguably the more valuable half: whether rebar's two-leg `fcntl.flock` + `mkdir`
locking design matches, exceeds, or falls short of what mature projects do for high local
concurrency, and whether the right fix is timeouts at all rather than a contention policy
(bounded retry with jitter, fail-fast-and-let-the-caller-retry, or queueing).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The OSS research findings are recorded on this ticket and the chosen approach cites them
      rather than asserting a value.
- [ ] Each local-only git call site either gets an explicit bound justified against LOCAL latency
      (not copied from the 300s network value), or is documented as deliberately unbounded with the
      reason stated.
- [ ] A timeout/contention failure produces an ACTIONABLE error naming what was contended and the
      remedy — not a bare exception. Converting one confusing failure into another is not progress.
- [ ] rebar's blocking policy under local contention is stated explicitly (block / bounded retry /
      fail fast), justified against the research, and applied consistently.
- [ ] `_commands/fsck.py` is either coordinated with bug 01e8 or split out and marked blocked on it.
- [ ] make lint, make typecheck, and the default suite exit zero.
data.title: Local-only git call sites are unbounded under high concurrent local use; contention policy is unspecified
